To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) RNNs trained with gradient-based learning can learn to chain together motor ‘motifs’, and 2) the brain’s motor thalamocortex might be a key component of the neural circuit that enables this chaining.
the brain’s motor thalamocorticocortical circuit is a good inductive bias for RNNs to learn to hierarchically produce motor motifs.

(1) a recurrent neural network architecture with a specific thalamocortic inductive bias can efficiently learn a large library of motor ‘motifs’, which can then be chained together to generate complex behavior, (2) this network architecture can learn these motor motifs without interference between them, and can chain them together in novel ways without any additional training, (3) this architecture can be used to model the function of motor circuits in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of continual learning of autonomous motor motifs, and how to improve their accuracy and robustness by incorporating brain insights.
the problem of learning hierarchical dynamics that produce complex behavior by reusing a small number of motor primitives (motifs), and with the problem of zero-shot chaining of these primitives.
the development of RNNs that can learn a library of motor motifs that are re-usable in arbitrary orders, and that can be chained together in new ways at test time without any additional training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed architecture and training scheme lead to a novel, accurate and robust RNN that can be trained with gradient-descent, and can produce hierarchical motor sequences in an efficient, extendable, accurate and robust way.
the proposed RNNs are able to learn a library of autonomous, hierarchical, and re-usable motor motifs, and to chain these motifs in arbitrary orders with no performance penalty.

we have developed a novel architecture for RNNs that can be efficiently and extendibly trained to produce complex, hierarchically structured, continuous outputs, while also improving the robustness of these RNNs to out-of-distribution conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to train recurrent neural networks that learn to produce complex behaviors by chaining together re-usable sub-behaviors (motor motifs) in arbitrary order.
the brain uses a thalamocortico-thalamocortical feedback loop to generate hierarchical motor behavior.
the motor system is a continual learner that uses a thalamocortically-inspired inductive bias to generate new behavior by chaining together previously learned motifs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the brain’s ability to learn new motor behaviors in an incremental fashion is enabled not only by the continual learning of new motor motifs but also by the ability to chain them in arbitrary orders without the need to retrain on the transitions between them.
the brain’s motor preparation system may be a key component in learning and executing complex behavior.

, in the absence of specific training data for the chaining of motifs, the brain uses an inductive bias to constrain the dynamics of the motor system in order to make it more likely to generate the correct motor transitions.
